doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Family album
summary: Laws recalls the success of Family, with his arrangements and constant orders for the record.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Okay, so it was a quartet. We’re going to jump ahead to 1980 and Family.

That’s one, boy. That was another. Frankie Crocker in New York, he had it on high rotation, and it just – all over. That record did really – in fact, we still perform that. Just performed it in Manila.
Because you have Ravel’s Bolero, What a Night!, Wildfire, Family, Memory of Minnie (Riperton), Say You’re Mine.

That’s it, and I did all the arrangements on that, all, everything. That’s what I was glad to be, because I feel like I was – I was really kind of nervous about that, because I remember Maurice Spears was doing the copying for me on that. I said, man, I don’t

know if this is going to come out all right, but it came out real well. To this day, we still – because we have a – on the website. That record still is ordered all the time, I mean, strong, all over the world. There’s no real connection. It’s like nobody played the record in this place and all of a sudden they’re going to order it. No, it just constantly comes in. So there must be something else that’s magnetizing those people to that record.
I think this is when I saw you bring the Laws family up to Berkeley.
The family? Maybe so. It could have been.
Yeah, it must have been around then.
